# Library acquisition review


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Struct editor visit and block-driven batching; confirmation capability and receipt record separate view/resource ownership.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

checkpoints: After each edit, no store write occurs until the visit has had a 120 ms quiet interval.
At the 120 ms checkpoint, exactly the latest text from that editing burst is written.
After a burst is saved, a later edit starts a new independently saveable burst.
Closing, replacing, or disposing a visit does not lose its latest edited text.
Preview behavior remains a separate 40 ms trailing task and is unchanged.

forbidden_effects: Do not write once per keystroke.
Do not publish superseded intermediate text from the same editing burst.
Do not let a retired visit's delayed task write into or otherwise act as a newer visit.
Do not change the synchronous workspace API or injected interfaces.
Do not change the adjacent search preview.
Do not merge editor-visit ownership with confirmation-outlet ownership.
Do not move storage, queue delivery, outlet, or command-state execution into native RPC.
lifecycle_identity: Every call to open creates a fresh CatalogVisit identity, including when reopening the same document id.
The editor trailing task belongs to the CatalogVisit/block for which it was created.
A subsequent edit burst on the same live visit reuses a functional trailing task after the preceding burst has flushed.
A Confirmation outlet owns the visit active when the outlet is acquired and remains active only while that exact visit is current.
Store subscription tokens belong to their visits and are stopped when those visits retire.

obligations.text: Workspace#edit must update the selected visit's in-memory text synchronously but schedule persistence through that visit's trailing task instead of writing immediately.
Editor persistence must use a 120 ms trailing quiet interval and write only the latest text supplied during each burst.
After one burst flushes, subsequent edit bursts must still schedule and save correctly.
Visit retirement must preserve the latest edited text and must not allow delayed work owned by the retired visit to interfere with a later visit.

The public methods open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), and dispose() remain synchronous and keep their existing return behavior, including submit returning the queue receipt or nil with no selected editor.
Submission continues to capture the current visit's in-memory snapshot, so it can synchronously submit the latest edit even before delayed store persistence occurs.
Opening or returning to a document creates a fresh visit, reads persisted text, renders that document, and installs only that visit's store subscription.
Confirmation output remains bound to the visit active when confirmation is acquired and is emitted only if that exact visit remains current after capture callbacks complete.
Dispose continues to detach integrations before the workspace is closed.
Preview query/hide behavior, including its independent 40 ms quiet interval and cancellation of unpublished preview work, remains unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Within edit, copy/freeze and assign the new text to the current visit before scheduling the trailing write.
